series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm/mempolicy: use SRCU for the weighted interleave state
series_items.patch_summary: This patch replaces the current implementation of weighted interleave state management in the Linux kernel's memory policy module with a new approach using SRCU (Schedulable RCU) to pin the global iw_table object and use it in-place. This change allows for more efficient handling of concurrent updates to the weights, reducing the need for synchronization and improving performance. The patch also introduces a new mechanism for retiring the weighted interleave state, which involves calling SRCU for sleeping readers and kfree_rcu for reference-less ones. The changes were tested with various configurations and tools, including KASAN, PROVE_LOCKING, and DEBUG_OBJECTS_RCU_HEAD.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/mempolicy: stop copying the nodemask in the interleave paths
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes the unnecessary copying of a nodemask in interleave node selectors, reducing memory usage and improving performance. The copy was only used to ensure consistency between the node count and the walk, but this is no longer necessary as bounds checking can be used instead. If an empty nodelist or weight is detected, the code falls back to using numa_node_id(). This change also removes a now-unused function read_once_policy_nodemask() and results in significant reductions in stack usage for certain functions.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to eliminate unnecessary copies of nodemasks and node weights in the interleave paths, improving performance by reducing memory allocation and synchronization overhead.

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: Raised a div-by-zero concern in alloc_pages_bulk_interleave() and suggested testing the patch series.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Fri, 28 Aug 2026 21:59:41 -0400 Gregory Price <gourry@gourry.net> wrote:

> The interleave node selectors and bulk allocators take copies of
> nodemasks and node weights (for weighted interleave) in the fault path.
> Both of these copies can be entirely eliminated.
> 
> For node weights, use SRCU to pin the weights in place.  This eliminates
> a copy and a kmalloc from the bulk allocator path.
> 
> For nodemasks, we can operate directly on pol->nodes as long as we bounds
> check the walk.  A concurrent rebind can shrink the mask, or tear the read
> of it so the mask appears empty.
> 
>  - The interleave node selectors fall back to numa_node_id() when that
>    happens, which is what they already did when a copy came back empty.
> 
>  - The bulk allocator simply returns what it managed to allocate.
> 
> The node count and weight totals are read separately from the nodemask
> walk that consumes them - creating a time-of-check / time-of-use race.
> Just clamp the walk to a single pass (number of nodes), and clamp each
> bulk allocation chunk to the space left in the request.
> 
> The cost is distribution accuracy during a rebind.  The copies never
> corrected for that either - they only kept the code from dividing by
> zero and overrunning the allocation request.

Not very well, it seems.  Sashiko thinks there's a div-by-zero in
alloc_pages_bulk_interleave().

	https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260829015943.1258774-1-gourry@gourry.net

> Gregory Price (2):
>   mm/mempolicy: use SRCU for the weighted interleave state
>   mm/mempolicy: stop copying the nodemask in the interleave paths

Looks nice, thanks - I'll queue it for testing.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm/huge_memory: skip zone device folios in madvise_free_huge_pmd()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the madvise_free_huge_pmd() function to skip zone device folios when performing lazyfree operations. The existing guards in this function do not cover all cases of zone device memory, and adding a check for zone device folios ensures that these areas are properly handled. This change addresses an issue where THP migration of zone device pages was not being filtered correctly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] mm/madvise: skip zone device folios in cold/pageout PMD range
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where zone device folios are not properly filtered in the madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() function, leading to potential double-put bugs. The patch adds a check for zone device memory and skips it during MADV_COLD/PAGEOUT operations.

review_comments.author: Balbir Singh
review_comments.summary: Identified that the patch makes sense and added a Reviewed-by tag.
review_comments.raw_body:
On 8/18/26 8:08 AM, Gregory Price wrote:
> madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range() resolves the folio backing a PMD
> via pmd_folio() and ages or reclaims it without checking for zone
> device memory.
> 
> The surrounding guards do not cover every zone device case:
> 
>   - can_madv_lru_vma() excludes VM_PFNMAP and VM_HUGETLB VMAs
>     (so device DAX is filtered)
> 
>   - !pmd_present() branch above rejects device-private and
>     migration entries, which are non-present.
> 
>   - A present zone device PMD - e.g. a device-coherent THP - is
>     not filtered by any of these, nor by pmd_folio() (unlike
>     vm_normal_page_pmd(), it performs no special/pfnmap check),
>     and would be aged or paged out here.
> 
> Skip ZONE_DEVICE folios explicitly during MADV_COLD/PAGEOUT.
> 
> Fixes: a30b48bf1b24 ("mm/migrate_device: implement THP migration of zone device pages")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
> Acked-by: David Hildenbrand (Arm) <david@kernel.org>
> Reviewed-by: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM) <ljs@kernel.org>
> ---
>  mm/madvise.c | 3 +++
>  1 file changed, 3 insertions(+)
> 
> diff --git a/mm/madvise.c b/mm/madvise.c
> index c179938097bf0..2151bb9468594 100644
> --- a/mm/madvise.c
> +++ b/mm/madvise.c
> @@ -396,6 +396,9 @@ static int madvise_cold_or_pageout_pte_range(pmd_t *pmd,
>  
>  		folio = pmd_folio(orig_pmd);
>  
> +		if (folio_is_zone_device(folio))
> +			goto huge_unlock;
> +
>  		/* Do not interfere with other mappings of this folio */
>  		if (folio_maybe_mapped_shared(folio))
>  			goto huge_unlock;

Makes sense

Reviewed-by: Balbir Singh <balbirs@nvidia.com>

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] mm/mempolicy: skip zone device folios when queueing folios
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where zone device folios are not properly filtered when queueing folios for migration. The patches add explicit checks to skip zone device folios in the `queue_folios_pte_range` and `queue_folios_pmd` functions, ensuring that only valid folios are processed. This fix is necessary because existing checks do not reject zone device memory, leading to incorrect behavior.

review_comments.author: Balbir Singh
review_comments.summary: A similar patch was sent out earlier for zone device private THP, and this patch makes sense. However, it should be noted that migration of device coherent THP is not supported yet.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Mon, Aug 17, 2026 at 06:08:10PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> queue_folios_pte_range() already pairs vm_normal_folio() with an
> explicit folio_is_zone_device() check before adding folios to the
> migration pagelist.
> 
> vm_normal_folio() alone does not reject zone device memory (a present
> device-coherent page in a normal VMA is returned as "normal").
> 
> Mirror the explicit check in queue_folios_pmd() as well.
> 
> queue_folios_pmd() uses pmd_folio() directly and can encounter a present
> zone device PMD - e.g. a device-coherent THP.
> 
> This is not filtered by existing checks:
>   !pmd_present()   - only rejects non-present device-private and
>                      migration entries
> 
>   vma_migratable() - excludes DAX and VM_PFNMAP.
> 
> The early return also means such a folio is no longer counted in
> qp->nr_failed under MPOL_MF_STRICT.  This is the same pattern used
> by queue_folios_pte_range() (skipping zone device without failing).
> 
> Fixes: a30b48bf1b24 ("mm/migrate_device: implement THP migration of zone device pages")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>

> index 3498a5651d50f..3418b5664dcf8 100644
> --- a/mm/mempolicy.c
> +++ b/mm/mempolicy.c
> @@ -662,6 +662,8 @@ static void queue_folios_pmd(pmd_t *pmd, struct mm_walk *walk)
>  		return;
>  	}
>  	folio = pmd_folio(pmdval);
> +	if (folio_is_zone_device(folio))
> +		return;
>  	if (is_huge_zero_folio(folio)) {
>  		walk->action = ACTION_CONTINUE;
>  		return;
> -- 
> 2.53.0-Meta
>


A similar patch was sent out earlier, but that was only for zone device
private THP, we don't support migration of device coherent THP today (we
should add support). The patch itself makes sense

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series adds missing checks to prevent zone device memory from being reclaimed, aged, or migrated in certain mm walkers. The existing checks only filtered out non-present device-private entries, but did not account for present zone device PMDs. The patches add explicit checks after the folio is resolved and before it is acted upon, ensuring correctness and hardening the kernel against potential issues.

review_comments.author: Lance Yang
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Lance Yang successfully tested the patch series on x86_64 QEMU and confirmed that it fixes a kernel panic issue when using PMD-mapped device-coherent THPs, but noted that without these patches, partial MADV_FREE and MADV_COLD operations would reliably hit a kernel panic in remove_migration_pte()
review_comments.raw_body:
Cool!

Gave the whole series a spin on x86_64 QEMU with a PMD-mapped
device-coherent THP. Without these patches, partial MADV_FREE and
MADV_COLD reliably hit a kernel panic in remove_migration_pte(), while
mbind(MPOL_MF_MOVE | MPOL_MF_STRICT) returned -EIO.

With v2, all three worked fine, PMD mapping stayed intact, and data
checked out :)

Note that both kernels used the same small change to the in-kernel HMM
test driver, allowing its coherent device memory to be allocated as 2 MB
folios so the PMD-mapped test case could be exercised.

Tested-by: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledges that the patch still has an issue with device-coherent memory, which was previously thought to be resolved.
review_comments.raw_body:
Yeah IIRC that was Usama's and I got confused thinking this had already
been resolved - but i realized this still affects device coherent.

ty!

~Gregory

review_comments.author: Andrew Morton
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton questioned the urgency of pushing this series to -stable, suggesting it could be treated as a leisurely next-merge-window thing rather than an immediate hotfix.
review_comments.raw_body:
Thanks Lance, you're so diligent.

I'm wondering what to do here.  Gregory told us

: No crash reproducer - this is a correctness/hardening cleanup found by
: inspection. All checks are placed after the folio is resolved and before
: it is acted upon, on paths that already hold the relevant page-table lock,
: so no locking or refcount changes are involved.

And you had to tweak the hmm-test driver to reproduce the bug(s).

So when do we push this series out to -stable?  As a hair-on-fire
hotfix, or as a leisurely next-merge-window thing?


And Sashiko was clearly having a bad day, able to find only nine
pre-existing things to shout about:
	https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20260817220810.1175596-1-gourry@gourry.net

review_comments.author: Lance Yang
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Lance Yang noted that the crash is real only when a PMD-mapped device-coherent folio exists and suggested delaying the patch's merge until the next window.
sentiment_signals: no need to rush this one
review_comments.raw_body:
Thanks, Andrew :) Yeah, I'd say next merge window should be fine :)

The crash is real once the mapping exists, but I had to tweak test_hmm
to create that PMD-mapped device-coherent folio, and I couldn't find
any in-tree production driver doing that today.

So no need to rush this one, I guess.

review_comments.author: Lance Yang
review_comments.summary: Lance Yang noted that the ZONE_DEVICE split handling only covers device-private folios and not device-coherent ones, which are not supported yet; he added checks in folio_check_splittable() and folio_split_unmapped() to reject device-coherent folios with an error code -EOPNOTSUPP.
review_comments.raw_body:
BTW, noticed that the ZONE_DEVICE split handling only covers
device-private folios, so device-coherent folios aren't supported ...

The call chains are:

split_folio()
  -> __folio_split()
    -> folio_check_splittable()
    -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

migrate_vma_pages()
  -> __migrate_device_pages()
    -> migrate_vma_split_unmapped_folio()
      -> folio_split_unmapped()
        -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

And I added the device-coherent check to folio_check_splittable() and
folio_split_unmapped(). See below. They can go away once device-coherent
folio splitting is supported :)

If folks think it's worth having, I can send it as a follow-up :)

---8<---
Subject: [PATCH] mm/huge_memory: don't split device-coherent folios

From: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>

The ZONE_DEVICE split handling only covers device-private folios.
Device-coherent folios are not supported.

The call chains are:

split_folio()
  -> __folio_split()
    -> folio_check_splittable()
    -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

migrate_vma_pages()
  -> __migrate_device_pages()
    -> migrate_vma_split_unmapped_folio()
      -> folio_split_unmapped()
        -> __folio_freeze_and_split_unmapped()

Reject device-coherent folios in folio_check_splittable() and
folio_split_unmapped().

Fixes: a30b48bf1b24 ("mm/migrate_device: implement THP migration of zone device pages")
Signed-off-by: Lance Yang <lance.yang@linux.dev>
---
 mm/huge_memory.c | 14 +++++++++++---
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/mm/huge_memory.c b/mm/huge_memory.c
index 54494c3fa983..a5dd38e9a8de 100644
--- a/mm/huge_memory.c
+++ b/mm/huge_memory.c
@@ -3937,6 +3937,10 @@ int folio_check_splittable(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order,
 	if (!folio->mapping && !folio_test_anon(folio))
 		return -EBUSY;

+	/* TODO: Support splitting device-coherent folios. */
+	if (folio_is_device_coherent(folio))
+		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
+
 	/* order-1 is not supported for anonymous THP. */
 	if (folio_test_anon(folio) && new_order == 1)
 		return -EINVAL;
@@ -4354,15 +4358,16 @@ static int __folio_split(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order,
  *
  * anon_vma_lock is not required to be held, mmap_read_lock() or
  * mmap_write_lock() should be held. @folio is expected to be locked by the
- * caller. device-private and non device-private folios are supported along
+ * caller. device-private and non-ZONE_DEVICE folios are supported along
  * with folios that are in the swapcache. @folio should also be unmapped and
  * isolated from LRU (if applicable)
  *
  * Upon return, the folio is not remapped, split folios are not added to LRU,
  * free_folio_and_swap_cache() is not called, and new folios remain locked.
  *
- * Return: 0 on success, -EAGAIN if the folio cannot be split (e.g., due to
- *         insufficient reference count or extra pins).
+ * Return: 0 on success, -EOPNOTSUPP for device-coherent folios, or -EAGAIN if
+ *         the folio cannot be split (e.g., due to insufficient reference
+ *         count or extra pins).
  */
 int folio_split_unmapped(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order)
 {
@@ -4373,6 +4378,9 @@ int folio_split_unmapped(struct folio *folio, unsigned int new_order)
 	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_FOLIO(!folio_test_large(folio), folio);
 	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE_FOLIO(!folio_test_anon(folio), folio);

+	if (folio_is_device_coherent(folio))
+		return -EOPNOTSUPP;
+
 	if (folio_expected_ref_count(folio) != folio_ref_count(folio) - 1)
 		return -EAGAIN;

--

Cheers, Lance

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledges that the split checks are worth it and appreciates the reviewer's testing efforts, indicating no need for further revision.
review_comments.raw_body:
First - thank you for testing, I was struggling to figure out a way to
test this and I somehow missed your email where you managed it.

Second - I think the split checks are worth it.  As I've worked through
my private node series, I've learned there are at least a handful of
missing zone device hooks throughout mm - but there is a lot of nuance
between the modes that is frustrating to keep straight.

Every zone device patch helps clarify how coherent-link accelerators
might manage its memory as a numa node, so at the very least I
appreciate it.

~Gregory
